rules.text: If the percentages inscribed inside the pie slices are intended to encode comparable shares of global energy consumption, and each inscription is attached to its named source category, then the category with the greatest printed percentage is the largest category; if that category has a matching priority-monitoring route, that route fulfills the stated routing criterion.
rules.conditions: This bridge depends on treating the printed slice percentages as authoritative and comparable global-consumption shares, and on the route label matching the identified category.

rules.text: If the angular extent or area of each pie slice is intended to encode comparable shares of global energy consumption, and the source name printed inside each slice identifies that slice, then the visibly largest slice represents the largest category; if that category has a matching priority-monitoring route, that route fulfills the stated routing criterion.
rules.conditions: This bridge depends on pie-slice geometry rather than the printed percentages being the authoritative encoding, and on the visibly largest slice being identifiable by its inscription.

rules.text: When a pie chart's printed percentage inscriptions and its slice geometry indicate different rankings, the largest global energy consumption category is not established from the chart alone unless it is determined which encoding is authoritative; a route choice based on either disputed ranking remains conditionally supported.
rules.conditions: This applies because both printed percentages and slice sizes are visible potential encodings of the same category shares, with no visible statement resolving a disagreement between them.
